# Agent Friendly Web - public context

## External verification AF-EV

AF-EV is orthogonal to the proprietary AF-0 to AF-5 maturity method. The Cloudflare `isitagentready.com` baseline observed on 2026-08-30 scored `agentfriendlyweb.dev` at 53/100, Level 2 Bot-Aware. This is a dated third-party diagnostic, not a certification, security assurance, indexing guarantee or ranking guarantee. The machine-readable history is published at `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/.well-known/external-readiness.json` and the human explanation at `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/verificacion-externa`.

After Sites version 27, a second provider observation returned Level 4 Agent-Integrated and passed Markdown negotiation, ARD and WebMCP. The provider API did not return a numeric score for that observation, so Agent Friendly Web does not infer one. DNS, OAuth, A2A and commerce remain separate gates and are not advertised merely to improve an external result.

## Identity

Agent Friendly Web is an initiative created by Gabriel Mucchiut and incubated within the Tokenizart infrastructure. Tokenizart is its first integral case study.

## Purpose

The service helps website owners understand what public agents can currently discover, what context is missing, and which technical or editorial change should happen next. It combines a public read-only audit with an authenticated, progressive owner dossier.

## Methodology

The AF-0 to AF-5 method scores seven evidence layers: discovery, answerability, machine-readable content, tools, experimental web interaction, trust/governance, and agentic commerce. Recommendations do not increase a score until implementation is publicly observable.

## AEO and crawler policy

The public guide at `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/aeo-y-crawlers` explains how answer engine optimization complements SEO. It separates search discovery, user-requested retrieval, model training and other generative-AI controls. The machine-readable catalog at `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/.well-known/crawler-policy-catalog.json` links each entry to an official provider source and distinguishes crawler user agents from robots.txt product tokens such as Google-Extended.

## Sector and language guidance

The first multilingual content slice is published in Spanish, English and Portuguese at `/sectores`, `/en/sectors` and `/pt/setores`. It explains how the same evidence discipline changes for art and collections, museums, institutions, commerce, SaaS and professional services.

## Measurement and assisted intake

The public comparison at `/medir-mejora` processes manually entered before/after values in the browser and does not persist them. It compares evidence and never guarantees ranking or recommendation. The prototype at `/asistente` deterministically proposes field-scoped intake values from rough text. It rejects likely credentials, requires human selection and does not save, email, charge or modify a website.

## Public conversational guide

The deployed public guide at `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/guia` answers from an allowlisted public topic and source catalog. It recognizes immediate continuations, adapts between simple, standard and detailed explanations, and links evidence for each answer. Conversation state exists only in React memory and clears on reload. It does not use an external model, access private projects, run audits or CLI commands, send email, execute payments or modify websites. Its project-specific boundary contract is published at `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/.well-known/public-guide-contract.json`.

## Open knowledge distribution

The public page at `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/conocimiento-abierto` explains the read-only OKF v0.2 release. The canonical bundle index is `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/okf/v0.2/index.md` and the distribution inventory is `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/okf/v0.2/manifest.json`. Concepts include source provenance, generated and verified timestamps, lifecycle status and an absolute freshness boundary. `CHECKSUMS.sha256` supports independent integrity checks. The manifest and AI Catalog links are Agent Friendly Web project extensions; they are not universal discovery endpoints required by OKF.

## Read-only CLI

The deployed repo-first CLI is documented at `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/cli`. Its machine manifest is `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/.well-known/agent-friendly-cli.json` and its response schema is `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/schemas/cli-response.v1.json`. It audits public sites, reads already-published Registry profiles and verifies OKF releases in memory. It performs no local or remote writes, uses no credentials and is not an MCP or A2A service.

## MCP public read-only deployed

The deployed service documented at `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/mcp-readonly` exposes `POST https://mcp.agentfriendlyweb.dev/mcp` through stateless Streamable HTTP. It contains exactly four public read-only tools for audit, methodology, published Registry profiles and canonical OKF v0.2 verification, plus four versioned `afw://` resources. Its discovery card is `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` and its stable result schema is `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/schemas/mcp-result.v1.json`.

The service uses no OAuth because it exposes public data only. It has no A2A delegation, private expedients, owner data, website mutations or payment actions. The separate deployed WebMCP browser tool exposes only `afw.audit_public_site` from the public page and reuses the public audit API. Modern MCP 2026-07-28 and stateless 2025 compatibility were verified with remote clients against the exact production Worker version before promotion.

## Publication capsule

Block 5A deploys a private manual-handoff workflow. It creates one immutable package with exact files, allowlisted destination paths, contents, SHA-256 hashes, expiration and human decisions bound to the manifest. Its public contracts are `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/schemas/publication-capsule.v1.json` and `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/schemas/capsule-decision.v1.json`.

This workflow no aplica cambios remotos: it does not access a CMS, open a Draft PR, use credentials, deploy code or advertise an A2A service. Real adapters, current-file textual diffs, operational rollback and any website write remain behind later gates.

## Block 5B deployed with remote submission disabled

The deployed private Block 5B workflow compares one approved capsule against only five allowlisted public destinations: `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` and `/`. It limits redirects, response time, bytes and diff lines; classifies partial failures without reflecting probable secrets; and keeps manual integrations separate from direct file proposals.

After human review, the owner may prepare and download an `agentfriendly.draft-pr-plan.v1` document. Its state is always `prepared_not_submitted`, `remoteSubmission` is `false` and `mergeAllowed` is `false`. The additive D1 migration is deployed, but GitHub authorization, Draft PR creation, merge, deployment and every target-site write remain behind later gates.

## Standards status

- robots.txt, sitemaps, Schema.org/JSON-LD and OpenAPI are treated as stable foundations.
- MCP 2026-07-28 is the current protocol reference used by this release.
- llms.txt is a community proposal.
- WebMCP is a W3C Community Group draft and remains experimental.
- x402 and MPP are emerging payment mechanisms that require case-specific technical, legal and commercial controls.

## Security

The public scanner accepts only public HTTP/HTTPS targets, rejects credentials and alternate ports, checks DNS resolution, limits time and response size, and does not follow redirects. It never mutates the target. The owner dossier never asks for credentials and stores only allowlisted context behind Sign in with ChatGPT.

## Tokenizart

Tokenizart is documented as an evolving agent-first architecture. Existing public content, Tokenizart-specific release-candidate CLI/MCP/skills, and authenticated Owner Live capabilities are kept as separate maturity boundaries. Those Tokenizart artifacts are distinct from the deployed Agent Friendly Web read-only CLI. Unreleased or private tools are not represented as publicly available.

## Machine-readable catalogs

The deployed ARD-compatible draft manifest, its `ai-catalog.json` compatibility alias and the Agent Skills index point to public resources on this site. The API Catalog is a standards-based linkset pointing to the public OpenAPI document and the deployed MCP contract. No OAuth resource, A2A service or payment protocol is advertised by this release. WebMCP remains experimental despite being deployed and externally observed.

## Capability status

The machine-readable readiness manifest at `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/.well-known/agent-readiness.json` is the current capability ledger. Discovery resources, the public read-only audit API, the audit skill, the repo-first read-only CLI, the public stateless MCP read-only server, Markdown negotiation, ARD compatibility and the browser WebMCP tool are deployed. A2A remains planned and x402 remains research. Candidate, planned and research work does not count as deployed evidence until its production gate closes.

## Illustrative maturity comparisons

The page `https://agentfriendlyweb.dev/evolucion-agentica` demonstrates how clearer public evidence can improve the answer an agent is able to construct for a restaurant, municipality or Tokenizart. Examples are illustrative. They do not guarantee indexing, wording, ranking or recommendation by GPT, Gemini, Claude or another provider.
